translation_history.english: "Like some winged creature of the upper air, Paul ran his course, traversing the inhabited world in a circuit." Nicephorus Callistus, Ecclesiastical History, book 3, chapter 1. "As though winged, he ran through the whole inhabited world and drew it in as in a net." Greek Menaea, June 29.

latin_text: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Niceph. hist. eccles. lib. 12. cap. 34. Vix triginta annorum spatio et Romanos, et Persas, et Parthos, et Medos, et Indos, et Scythas, et Sauromatas, et Sarracenos, et omne prorsus humanum genus sub jugum mitteret veritatis, &c. Chrysost. homil. 4. de laudib. Pauli. Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios pag. 8. de eodem: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. In oriente ac occidente verbi præco factus, illustrem fidei suæ fainam sortitus est, in justitia mundum universum instruens, et ad occidentis terminos veniens, et sub imperatoribus martyrium subiens, sic e mundo migravit.

translation_history.english: "Having traversed nearly the whole earth, and having contended for Christ in the gospel for thirty-five years." Nicephorus, Ecclesiastical History, book 12, chapter 34. "In scarcely thirty years' span he brought under the yoke of truth the Romans, the Persians, the Parthians, the Medes, the Indians, the Scythians, the Sauromatae, the Saracens, and absolutely the whole human race, etc." Chrysostom, Homily 4 in Praise of Paul. Clement, in his Epistle to the Corinthians, page 8, says of the same man: "Having become a herald in the East and in the West, he obtained the noble renown of his faith, teaching righteousness to the whole world; and having come to the limit of the West, and having borne witness before the rulers, he thus departed from the world." "Made a herald of the word in the East and the West, he won an illustrious reputation for his faith, instructing the whole world in righteousness, and coming to the bounds of the West, and undergoing martyrdom under the emperors, thus he departed from the world."
translation_history.notes: Two Greek discrepancies in the printed text: 'fainam' is a typo for 'famam'; rendered as 'reputation/renown'.
